note: Saint Helena's one bank is the Bank of St Helena, and it offers a person there no credit card. Its About Us page (read 2026-11-03) says that since its establishment it has been the only banking facility on both St Helena Island and Ascension Island, and it is the only bank the banks research holds for Saint Helena. Its Rates, Fees and Charges of 1 April 2026 price savings, international payments, teller services, St Helena Pay and lending (unsecured personal lending at 8%, secured at 7%); the only card charges in it are a 3% Tourist Card cash withdrawal and a 5% cash advance (minimum £2.50) against a credit or debit card issued elsewhere. The cards it issues are all paid from money already held: the Local Debit Card, free on a personal or business current account and used through St Helena Pay; the Start Smart Card for teens aged 13 to 17; and the Tourist Card, a prepaid GBP card for visitors. Its banking information for visitors says credit and debit cards are not widely accepted for payment on St Helena and there are no ATMs. No page read says 'we issue no credit card' in so many words: the reading rests on the bank's whole tariff and its own list of cards, none of them a credit card. A St Helenian who banks with a bank abroad does so under that bank's terms, which this file doesn't cover.
